name: Scaling limiter, degree 1, extrema over the whole cell (2.9)
source: Zhang and Shu, J. Comput. Phys. 229 (2010), (2.8)-(2.11), Lemma 2.4, Theorem 2.5; Zhang and Shu, Proc. R. Soc. A 467 (2011), (2.9)-(2.10), Lemma 1

claims.why: avg(p~) = ubar + theta (avg(p) - ubar) = ubar for any scalar theta
p - ubar lies in [m_x - ubar, M_x - ubar] on the cell; theta <= |M - ubar|/|M_x - ubar| and <= |m - ubar|/|m_x - ubar| with ubar in [m, M], theta >= 0
without ubar in [m, M]: p = 1 + y/4, [m, M] = [-1, 0] gives theta = 1 and p~ = p > M everywhere (the average itself is outside, and p~ keeps it)
if theta < 1 by the upper term, |p~ - p| = (M_x - M)|p - ubar|/(M_x - ubar) <= C_k (M_x - M), C_k = sup max|q| / max q over zero-mean q of degree k, finite by compactness (the sources' proof)
